title: Fingerless gloves with partial finger tubes
subtitle: Fingerless gloves with short knuckle-length tubes on each finger.
excerpt: Fingerless gloves in DK wool with short individual finger tubes reaching to the base of the knuckles. Each finger is worked in a round from stitches divided from the hand. Gusseted thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Fingerless gloves with individual finger tubes built from the hand opening are documented across multiple contemporary knitting references. Construction synthesised from standard sock-yoke-style finger division methods documented in sock and glove knitting references.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A wedge of stitches added gradually on either side of a marker to build the thumb opening. The extra stitches follow the natural widening of the hand towards the base of the thumb. The gusset stitches are placed on hold while the hand is finished, then worked for the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Fingerless gloves in DK wool with short individual finger tubes reaching to the base of the knuckles. Each finger is worked separately in the round from stitches divided off the hand.
Thumb gusset
construction. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

The construction works cuff-up: cast on, work a rib cuff, increase the thumb gusset, work the hand, then divide and work the four finger tubes. Each finger uses about 10 stitches at DK gauge. The method uses
magic loop
throughout. Budget about 100 g (220 m / 240 yards) per pair in a smooth DK yarn. Fuzzy or hairy yarns make picking up stitches at the finger division harder.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 100 g (about 220 m / 240 yards) of DK-weight wool. Use a smooth, plied yarn.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 4: 1 for beginning of round, 2 to flank the thumb gusset, 1 to separate palm and back of hand during finger division

items.name: Scrap yarn or small stitch holders
items.qty: 4 lengths, about 30 cm each, to hold inactive finger stitches

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles. An accurate gauge is important here because finger circumferences are small and a few stitches matter.
Finger stitch counts

attrs.heading: Per finger (S / M / L). All worked in stocking stitch for 8 rounds.

content.text: Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 20 (22, 24) rounds of 2x2 rib.
Thumb gusset

Set up the thumb gusset on the palm side: knit to last 3 stitches of the palm, PM, k1, PM, knit to end. Gusset increase round: knit to marker, SM, M1L, knit to next marker, M1R, SM, knit to end. Knit 2 plain rounds. Repeat increases every 3rd round 4 (5, 5) more times. The gusset grows to 11 (13, 13) stitches. Work 2 plain rounds.
Place thumb on hold
Thread 11 (13, 13) gusset stitches onto scrap yarn. Cast on 3 stitches over the gap using the backward-loop cast-on. Continue in stocking stitch until the hand measures 2 cm short of the fingers.
Finger division
Place a midpoint marker separating the palm stitches from the back-of-hand stitches. Each finger uses stitches from both the palm half and the back-of-hand half.

Work the little finger first. Thread the little finger stitches (4 (4, 5) from palm, 4 (4, 5) from back) onto a short length of scrap yarn as a working needle. Cast on 1 stitch at the gap. Work 8 rounds in stocking stitch. Bind off. Repeat for ring, middle, and index fingers in sequence, picking up 1 or 2 bridge stitches at the gap between adjacent fingers as you work each one.
Thumb
Return 11 (13, 13) held gusset stitches to needles. Pick up 3 stitches from the gap. Work 10 (12, 12) rounds in stocking stitch. Bind off.
Common faults
Holes at the finger joins: not enough pick-up stitches at the bridge between fingers. Pick up 1 to 2 extra stitches at each gap and decrease them away on the first round.
Finger tubes are too tight: the stitch count for the size is at the lower end and your row gauge is tighter than average. Work one size up on fingers while keeping the hand at your size.
Finishing
Weave in all tails, paying particular attention to the finger join tails. Use your tapestry needle to close any remaining hole at each finger crotch.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. Block lightly to even out the join areas.
What to try next
The same cuff-up construction extended to full-length fingers produces a complete fitted glove. The finger-division technique is identical; only the length changes.
